strengths: Novel idea of achieving high-rank updates through progressive optimal scaling of low-rank adapters addresses real LoRA limitations (convergence, performance gap)
Rigorous theoretical analysis with closed-form analytical solutions (Theorems 3.5, 3.7) and rigorously proven sufficient/necessary conditions (Theorem 3.2)
Comprehensive experiments across diverse scales (184M-12B parameters) and tasks (GLUE, commonsense reasoning, mathematics) with consistent improvements and multiple baselines
Practical ScaLoRA-I variant achieves only 4% overhead while maintaining performance, with clear algorithm and good ablation studies (Tables 4, 11)
Strong empirical analysis demonstrating rank growth, stability justifying theoretical assumptions, and efficient moment estimator updates
Detailed experimental reproducibility documentation with hyperparameters, standard deviations across 3 runs, and thorough appendix
weaknesses: Gap between theory and practice: optimizes quadratic upper bound (Eq. 6) not actual loss; Theorem 3.2's necessary/sufficient conditions require prohibitively expensive O(Smnr) SVD computation with limited practical relevance

Theorem 3.7 applicability limited: requires non-negative solution to 2r×2r linear system, satisfied in ~80% of layers empirically; no theoretical justification for this pattern or principled handling of remaining 20%
No convergence rate guarantees or analysis of how merging strategy (Eq. 3) affects convergence properties; treats Lipschitz constant L as hyperparameter without theoretical guidance
Modest experimental improvements: 0.5% GLUE average gain, 0.3-1.0% commonsense reasoning gains often within standard deviation; no statistical significance testing despite small effect sizes

Fair comparison concerns: different methods use substantially different learning rates (HiRA 10× higher); differential hyperparameter tuning effort across baselines raises questions about fair comparison
Limited analysis of when high-rank updates help: no systematic study of task properties determining ScaLoRA benefit; gains vary from negligible to 1% without clear characterization
Introduces additional hyperparameter I (ScaLoRA-I) with performance sensitive to choice (Table 10: significant drops for I>10); no principled tuning method provided

Incomplete treatment of practical constraints: storage of full merged matrices W_t dismissed as 'disk abundant' without analyzing deployment scenarios or multi-task fine-tuning; code availability not mentioned
